laws.rule: After a warning is ignored, the police can fine anyone who goes bare-chested in public, shouts in a place that must stay quiet, jumps a queue (including for lifts) or grabs another person's seat on public transport (article 55). City-management fines also apply for spitting, urinating in public and littering (article 63), scribbling or carving on property and putting up ads (article 65), and smoking in banned places after being asked to stop (article 64). Dogs must be on a lead and droppings cleared (article 71).
laws.penalty_signal: Article 55: CNY 50 to 200 (about A$10.67 to A$42.66). Spitting, urinating or littering: CNY 50 to 200 (about A$10.67 to A$42.66); throwing objects from a building: CNY 500 (about A$107) (article 63). Smoking: CNY 50 to 200 (about A$10.67 to A$42.66) (article 64). Scribbling or carving: CNY 100 to 200 (about A$21.33 to A$42.66), or CNY 2,000 (about A$427) where it harms the city's appearance (article 65). Dog off the lead: CNY 100 to 500 (about A$21.33 to A$107); droppings not cleared: CNY 50 to 200 (about A$10.67 to A$42.66) (article 71). (CNY at 4.6877 per A$1, RBA 30 Oct 2026.)
laws.heading: 天津市文明行为促进条例 (Tianjin Civilised Behaviour Promotion Regulation)

laws.rule: Setting off fireworks is banned inside the Outer Ring Road (including the road) and, outside it, near bridges, tunnels, power and gas facilities and other listed places (item 1). It is banned across the whole city during heavy air-pollution emergency response (item 2). The decision came into force on 15 August 2026.
laws.penalty_signal: Fine CNY 100 to 500 (about A$21.33 to A$107) (item 8). (CNY at 4.6877 per A$1, RBA 30 Oct 2026.)
